messages:
Anna: quick heads-up — saw a correctness blip when compaction kicked while eviction was demoting prefixes. small repro in canary.
Ben: ugh. which invariant broke?
Anna: read-after-write on a recently-demoted prefix. request hit new owner + KV snapshot lagged, returned stale KV and then we applied newer write — client observed regressed tokens.
Chandra: so prefix moved, compaction simultaneously rewrote tombstones, and eviction removed residency before handoff finished?
Anna: yeah. timeline: lease revoke -> demote -> compaction scan -> eviction removes slab -> new owner tries to rebuild -> sees compacted tombstones, thinks prefix empty.
Kyra: can you paste the minimal trace/log lines?
Anna: pasted below (trimmed):
```
[3185554321] lease_revoke(prefix=tenantA/0x1a)
[3185554323] demote_start(prefix=tenantA/0x1a, epoch=42)
[3185554325] compaction_pass(prefix=tenantA/0x1a) // rewrote tombstones
[3185554330] eviction_free(slab=0x9f) // removed residency
[3185554332] new_owner_replay(prefix=tenantA/0x1a) -> no_keys
[3185554334] client_write(prefix=tenantA/0x1a, seq=100)
[3185554336] client_read(prefix=tenantA/0x1a) -> returns older seq=99
```
Ben: makes sense. we rely on demote -> handoff -> confirm residency removed only after checkpoint, but compaction blurred that boundary.
Chandra: two quick options: 1) treat compaction as a first-class participant in the handshake (block eviction until last compaction seq acknowledged) or 2) strengthen handoff to stash a small recovery log so new owner can reconcile with compacted tombstones.
Kyra: option 1 increases tail-latency during compaction peaks. option 2 adds a tiny write path on handoff but keeps compaction cheap.
Anna: leaning toward 2. we already have a delta-applier for prefix snapshot; extend it to carry compaction-anchors (compact_seq + tombstone_digest). new owner fetches anchor then replays small delta set if mismatch.
Ben: sketch of changes?
Chandra: handshake flow change (pseudocode):
```
HandoffInitiate -> publish {handoff_epoch, compact_anchor}
EvictWait -> wait for owners to ack compact_anchor
If owner missing -> owner reconstruct using delta pulled from origin (bounded by compact_anchor)
```
Kyra: we should also add a sanity-check metric: "handshake_compaction_mismatch_count" and alert when >0 for a few minutes.
Anna: agreed. I'll draft a tiny RFC + canary plan: small tenant in runbook, force compaction + handoff interleaving, assert no R/W regressions.
Ben: +1 on metrics. add e2e quick test that injects a tombstone rewrite during handoff.
Chandra: edgecases: what if origin already GC'd deltas beyond anchor? then fallback is to fallback to full prefix snapshot restore (expensive) — document and rate-limit.
Kyra: also we need to check Dedicated customers — private infra might have different compaction cadence. note in RFC.
ops-bot: deploy queued: prefix-handoff-safety-check (canary) -> scheduled 2026-03-22 03:00 UTC
Anna: thanks all. I'll drop a short RFC link when ready. tagging @Ben @Chandra for review. :thumbsup:
Ben: quick question for follow-up — can we keep the delta size bounded at O(prefix-changes-per-minute)? we shouldn't copy whole prefix.
Anna: yes, plan is to keep deltas incremental via change-log cursor bounded by compact_anchor. I'll spell limits in RFC.
Kyra: sounds good. leaving action items: Anna: RFC + canary plan. Ben: metrics + e2e test. Chandra: handshake pseudocode + fallback doc. I'll own Dedicated notes.
Anna: got it — will ping here when RFC is up.
